title: The future with will
subtitle: Decisions now, promises and what you think will happen
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: Use **will** when you **decide at the moment of speaking**, when you **promise** or **offer**, and when you say what you **think** will happen. For a plan you already have, use *be going to*.

blocks.label: Decisions now
blocks.title: You decide while you are speaking

examples.fr: I'm thirsty. I **will get** some water.
examples.en: No plan: the idea is new.

examples.fr: It's hot. I **will open** the window.
The phone is ringing. I **will answer** it.
Wait here. I **will ask** my mother.
That bag looks heavy. I **will carry** it.

blocks.label: What you think
blocks.title: After I think, I hope, maybe, probably

examples.fr: One day people **will live** on the moon.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.note: *Will* never changes and the verb after it never changes: *he will go*, not *he wills go*, not *he will goes*, not *he will to go*.

blocks.title: If and when
blocks.text: After **if** and **when**, use the **present simple**, not *will*. The other part of the sentence takes *will*.

examples.fr: If it **rains**, we **will stay** at home.
When I **get** home, I **will call** you.
If you **study**, you **will pass** the test.
I **will tell** her when I **see** her.

blocks.text: tomorrow, next week / year, soon, later, one day, in the future, in 2050, I think, I hope, I'm sure, maybe, probably, I promise …

examples.en: Yes, I will. / No, I won't.

examples.fr: **Will**: decided now. *“We have no rice.” “Oh! I will buy some.”*
**Going to**: decided before. *“We have no rice.” “I know. I am going to buy some.”*
**Will**: what I think. *I think our team will win.*
**Going to**: what I can see. *It is 3–0. Our team is going to win.*
